title: Shared Layouts: The _app.js Pattern
description: Wrap every page with a persistent header and footer using the custom App component.

slides.title: Why Do We Need Layouts? 🏗️
slides.content:
# The Repetition Problem

Every page likely needs a common **Header**, **Footer**, or **Sidebar**.

Without layouts, you'd repeat code in every page file – terrible for maintenance.

Next.js gives you a special component: **`pages/_app.js`**, which wraps every page automatically.

Think of it as the **outer shell** of your application. 🐚

slides.title: A Simple Layout in _app.js (pages/_app.js)
slides.content: Add a Header and Footer that appear on every single page.

quizData.question: What is the role of `pages/_app.js`?

options.text: It initializes pages and can wrap them with common layout components or global state
It's a special page for the app dashboard

quizData.explanation: `_app.js` is the top-level component that persists across page changes. It’s the perfect place for layouts, global CSS, and context providers.

slides.title: The Component Prop 🧩
slides.content:
# Understanding Component & pageProps

* `Component` – the active page (the file in `pages/` that matches the route).
* `pageProps` – an object with the props that the page's data fetching methods returned.

When you navigate, `Component` changes, but the wrapping `Header` and `Footer` stay the same. That's why React doesn't remount them – it's only the inner content that updates.

slides.title: A Header Component (components/Header.js)
slides.content: Simple navigation bar that sits on top of every page.

quizData.question: When you navigate from / to /about, what happens to the Header component defined in _app.js?

options.text: It stays mounted and doesn't re‑render
It only renders on the home page
It converts to a different component

quizData.explanation: Since the layout is around the `<Component>`, React sees only the inner component changed. The wrapping UI remains mounted, preserving state and avoiding extra work.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: You can also use `_app.js` to inject global context providers (Redux, Theme) or to trigger page transition animations. It's the central orchestrator of your app.
